To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stereotype activation is promoted by comprehension goals and stereotype application is promoted by self-enhancement goals.
people are more likely to stereotype a member of a stigmatized group when (a) they want to understand the person and (b) they want to feel good about themselves.
people tend to stereotype others more when they are trying to understand them and less when they are trying not to stereotype them.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes through which people come to know about the world and to make judgments about other people.
the question of how stereotypes influence our perceptions and judgments of other people.
how stereotypes are used to make sense of the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation and application of stereotypes during interaction is goal dependent.
stereotypes are activated when they can be used to help us understand a person's behavior or when they can be useful for self-enhancing purposes.
stereotypes are activated and applied in a wide variety of contexts and situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stereotype activation and application are goal-based phenomena.
stereotypes are activated and applied during interaction when they serve a comprehension goal or a self-enhancement goal, and when the motivation to avoid prejudice is weak or absent.
stereotype application is a function of both comprehension and self-enhancing goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

stereotypes are not automatically activated and applied during interaction, but that they are activated when they help us understand the person and are applied when doing so is consistent with our comprehension and self-enhancing goals.
people are not passive recipients of the stereotypes they hold; they are active processors of social information, and they can choose to stereotype their interaction partners or not.

the activation and application of stereotypes is goal-based, and that this goal-based perspective is useful for integrating a broad range of diverse findings on stereotype activation, application, and prejudice.
